rollCalls.title: Wyoming state guard-amendments.
rollCalls.summary: This act removes the requirement that the Wyoming National Guard must be activated into the service of the United States before the Wyoming State Guard may be organized and removes federal involvement in the Wyoming State Guard. This act allows the Governor to establish and maintain the Wyoming State Guard as necessary to preserve the public peace, execute the laws of the state, suppress tumult, riot, mob or invasion, respond to emergencies within the state, support national wildland fire response or perform other duties as the Governor may require.

rollCalls.title: Duties of registered agents-amendments.
rollCalls.summary: AN ACT relating to corporations, partnerships and associations; modifying the duties of registered agents; requiring registered agents to maintain the names of all owners of each entity; providing exceptions; and providing for an effective date.

rollCalls.title: Wyoming Indian Child Welfare Act sunset repeal.
rollCalls.summary: Currently, the Wyoming Indian Child Welfare Act (Act) is set to sunset (automatically repeal) on July 1, 2026. This legislation repeals that provision in the Act that would sunset the Act. Consequently, the Act will no longer have a sunset date.

rollCalls.title: Local approval for simulcasting.
rollCalls.summary: Under existing law, the Wyoming Gaming Commission issues permits for simulcasting of pari-mutuel wagering, which includes historic horse racing terminals, subject only to approval by the board of county commissioners. This act requires approval by the city, town or county where the simulcasting facility will be located before issuance or renewal of a simulcasting permit, and authorizes review and objection by overlapping local governments.

rollCalls.title: Hospital bankruptcy proceedings.
rollCalls.summary: This act allows county memorial hospitals and hospital districts to file for bankruptcy under Chapter 9 of the United States Bankruptcy Code, subject to specified requirements. A bankruptcy petition for a county memorial hospital must be approved by the applicable board of county commissioners. If approved, the board of trustees for a county memorial hospital may move forward with the petition. Hospital districts may apply for bankruptcy without a vote of qualified electors, but the trustees of the hospital district must advertise the motion to file for bankruptcy.

This program provides a reenlistment or extension bonus of not more than five thousand dollars ($5,000.00) to a Wyoming National Guard member who satisfies the Wyoming National Guard's reenlistment or extension eligibility criteria, reenlists or extends with the Wyoming National Guard for not less than three (3) years, and satisfies any other requirements specified by the Wyoming Military Department.

rollCalls.title: Eligibility for Medicaid-criteria.
rollCalls.summary: This act codifies current state criteria for Medicaid eligibility, including but not limited to requirements regarding citizenship, Wyoming residency, a determination of disability or an entitlement to receive social security income. rollCalls.title: State management-federal mineral leases.
rollCalls.summary: This joint resolution requests Congress to introduce a bill and enact law to amend the federal Mineral Leasing Act to authorize the state of Wyoming to administer and manage mineral leasing on federal lands located in Wyoming. This joint resolution specifically requests Congress to allow Wyoming to enter into cooperative agreements with the United States Secretary of Interior for Wyoming to assume administrative primacy for mineral leasing on specified federal lands located within Wyoming.

Requires cities, towns, special districts and counties to provide relevant data for the study. rollCalls.title: Water districts-funds for maintenance projects.
rollCalls.summary: This act authorizes irrigation districts, watershed improvement districts and water conservancy districts to allocate a portion of annual district funding for major maintenance projects. The act also allows water conservancy districts to assess one (1) additional mill for major maintenance projects. The act permits the investment of funds in major maintenance accounts with the state treasurer in local government investment equity pools. The act establishes that funds for major maintenance projects will be pooled until sufficient for project funding.

rollCalls.title: Good neighbor authority-amendments.
rollCalls.summary: This act removes the restriction on the number of additional employees that the Wyoming State Forester may hire for the Wyoming Good Neighbor Authority Program and authorizes these additional employees to be funded using any funds deposited in the Wyoming Good Neighbor Authority Revolving Account. This act authorizes grants, gifts, transfers, bequests, and donations to be deposited in the Wyoming State Forestry Good Neighbor Authority Revolving Account.

rollCalls.title: Department of revenue-electronic communication.
rollCalls.summary: This act changes how the Department of Revenue provides notices to taxpayers related to sales and use taxes. The act removes the requirement for certain notices to be sent by mail and specifies that written notice sent using the contact information provided by the taxpayer will fulfill notification requirements. The Department may send notices electronically if the taxpayer has provided electronic contact information. The act also makes conforming changes to related enforcement, compliance and penalty provisions.

rollCalls.title: Uniform mortgage modification act.
rollCalls.summary: This bill adopts the Uniform Mortgage Modification Act, establishing a framework for modifying mortgages and related obligations. The bill defines key terms such as "mortgage," "modification" and "obligation" and specifies the types of mortgage modifications covered by the act, including changes to interest rates, payment schedules and financial covenants. The bill ensures that a mortgage retains its priority and continues to secure the obligation after a mortgage modification, without requiring re-recording.

rollCalls.title: Fentanyl to minors-enhanced penalty.
rollCalls.summary: This act provides separate and enhanced penalties for persons who distribute fentanyl to minors. Any person who is at least age eighteen (18) and distributes fentanyl to a person under age eighteen (18) is guilty of a felony punishable by a fine specified in statute for certain controlled-substance offenses and imprisonment for up to twice the term authorized in W.S. 35-7-1031(a)(ii). The fine for this offense may be up to ten thousand dollars ($10,000.00), and the term of imprisonment may be up to twenty (20) years.

rollCalls.title: Theft amendments.
rollCalls.summary: This act amends the criminal offense of theft. The act amends the penalty for misdemeanor theft to be punishable by imprisonment for up to one (1) year (increased from six (6) months), a fine not to exceed one thousand five hundred dollars ($1,500.00) (increased from seven hundred fifty dollars ($750.00)), or both. The act also amends the offense threshold for felony theft. A person convicted of a third or subsequent theft offense (rather than the fifth offense) is guilty of felony theft.
